global_briefing: Keep three threads in view. Middle East shipping risk, from Houthi threats and the Saudi-led strike on a Yemeni port, raises diesel, freight and sulphur costs, squeezing Chilean SX-EW copper and Indonesian HPAL nickel through price before volume. Weaker equity markets and the AI-linked selloff could cut data-centre capex, weakening the copper and grid case at its edge. US chip export controls and AI chip approvals for China make data-centre demand depend on trade policy as much as on investment. European security spending after the Russian drone and missile incidents, and the Estonia border dispute, keeps defence budgets high and supports tungsten and antimony. Indonesia's fires, possibly linked to El Niño, are an unquantified supply risk for nickel through power, water and smoke.
